easy.def: A word for a boy or a man.
examples: He is my brother.
He plays the drums.
My dad said he is hungry.

more.def: A word used for a boy, a man, or a male animal that has already been talked about.
examples: My uncle lives far away, but he visits every summer.
The rooster crowed because he woke up early.
Ben said he would bring the soccer ball.

easy.def: The top part of your body with your face.
examples: I wear a hat on my head.
She nodded her head.
The dog shook its head.

more.def: The top part of the body, which holds the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.
examples: He put a helmet on his head before riding his bike.
The giraffe lifted its head high to reach the leaves.
She scratched her head while she thought.

easy.def: A pain in your head.
examples: I have a headache.
Noise gives me a headache.
The headache went away.

more.def: A pain in the head.
examples: I had a headache after being in the sun.
Loud noise can give you a headache.
Rest and water helped her headache go away.

easy.def: The main office of a group.
examples: The fire department headquarters is downtown.
The company headquarters is big.
The police headquarters is near the park.

more.def: The main place from which a group is controlled.
examples: The fire department headquarters is next to the park.
The company's headquarters is in a tall building.
Scouts meet at their headquarters on Fridays.

easy.def: To get better after being hurt.
examples: The cut will heal.
My arm healed.
The broken bone healed.

more.def: To become healthy again after being hurt or sick.
examples: The cut healed in a few days.
A broken bone takes weeks to heal.
The doctor helped the sick bird heal.

easy.def: How well your body is.
examples: Good food helps your health.
My health is good.
Exercise is good for health.

more.def: The condition of your body, and how well it works.
examples: Exercise is good for your health.
She is in good health.
Fresh fruit is good for your health.

easy.def: Well and strong, not sick.
examples: Eating fruit helps you stay healthy.
My puppy is healthy and strong.
Carrots are a healthy snack.

more.def: Having a strong body and mind; not ill. Also, good for your body.
examples: Exercise and sleep help keep you healthy.
The doctor said my teeth are healthy.
A healthy breakfast gives you energy for the morning.

easy.def: To take in sounds with your ears.
examples: I hear a bell.
She heard a bird.
Can you hear me?

more.def: To notice a sound with your ears, or to be told about something.
examples: We could hear the waves crashing from our tent.
Did you hear that our school won the contest?
I heard a strange noise coming from the attic.

easy.def: The ability to hear.
examples: Dogs have good hearing.
My hearing is good.
Bats have sharp hearing.

more.def: The sense that lets you hear sounds.
examples: Dogs have much better hearing than people.
Her hearing improved with a hearing aid.
Owls have sharp hearing.

easy.def: The part inside you that pumps blood.
examples: My heart beats.
Put your hand on your heart.
A heart is strong.

more.def: The body part in your chest that pumps blood around your body.
examples: Your heart beats faster when you run.
The doctor listened to my heart.
A whale has a heart as big as a small car.

easy.def: A shape that stands for love.
examples: She drew a heart.
I gave Mom a heart card.
The heart is red.

more.def: A shape with two round tops that comes to a point, used to show love.
examples: She drew a big red heart on the card.
The cookie was cut into the shape of a heart.
He gave his mother a paper heart.

easy.def: Warmth.
examples: The heat of the sun.
I feel the heat.
The heat is on.

more.def: The quality of being hot, or the warmth from something hot.
examples: The heat from the fire warmed the room.
We felt the heat of the sun on our faces.
The summer heat made us thirsty.

easy.def: To make hot.
examples: Heat the soup.
Mom heated the milk.
The sun heats the sand.

more.def: To make something warm or hot.
examples: Heat the soup on the stove.
The sun heated the sand.
Mom heated the milk for hot chocolate.

easy.def: A happy place that some people believe in.
examples: Some people believe in heaven.
Grandma says Grandpa is in heaven.
In the story, angels lived in heaven.

more.def: In some religions, the place where God lives and where good people go after death.
examples: Many people believe that heaven is a peaceful place.
The old song talked about a beautiful heaven.
She thinks her grandfather is in heaven.

easy.def: Hard to lift.
examples: This box of books is heavy.
The rock is too heavy to lift.
An elephant is very heavy.

more.def: Weighing a lot; hard to lift or move.
examples: The heavy backpack made his shoulders ache.
The truck carried a heavy load of bricks.
This winter coat is thick and heavy.

easy.def: A mild word for being surprised or upset.
examples: Oh, heck!
What the heck is that?
Heck, I forgot my hat.

more.def: A mild word that people say when they are surprised or a little bit upset.
examples: Oh heck, I left my lunch at home!
What the heck is that noise?
Heck, I almost missed the bus.

easy.def: The back part of your foot.
examples: My heel hurts.
The sock has a hole in the heel.
I stood on my heel.

more.def: The rounded back part of your foot, below your ankle.
examples: I got a blister on my heel.
The sock had a hole in the heel.
She stood on her heels to see over the crowd.

easy.def: How tall something is.
examples: What is your height?
The height of the tree is big.
Measure your height.

more.def: The distance from the bottom to the top of something.
examples: The nurse measured my height.
The height of the building is two hundred feet.
The plant grew to a height of three feet.

easy.def: A flying machine with spinning blades on top.
examples: The helicopter landed.
We saw a helicopter.
The helicopter flew low.

more.def: An aircraft that flies using large spinning blades on top, and can go straight up and down.
examples: The helicopter landed in the field.
A helicopter carried the hurt hiker to the hospital.
The helicopter's blades made a loud noise.

easy.def: A word you say when you meet someone.
examples: Hello, Mom!
Say hello to Grandpa.
Hello, my name is Ben.

more.def: A word used to greet someone or to start a phone call.
examples: Hello, how are you today?
She said hello to the new student with a smile.
I picked up the phone and said hello.

easy.def: A hard hat that protects your head.
examples: I wear a helmet on my bike.
The helmet is blue.
Put on your helmet.

more.def: A strong, hard hat that protects your head.
examples: I wear a helmet when I ride my bike.
The football player buckled his helmet.
Workers wear a helmet on the building site.

easy.def: To do something for someone to make it easier.
examples: I help my mom.
She helped him up.
Can you help me?

more.def: To make something easier or better for someone by doing part of the work.
examples: The children helped the teacher carry the boxes of books.
Rain helps the flowers grow in spring.
Neighbors came to help after the storm.

easy.def: Something you do to make things easier for someone.
examples: Thank you for your help.
I need help.
He asked for help.

more.def: The act of giving someone support, or anything that is useful to someone.
examples: The lost hiker called for help and the rangers came quickly.
My brother's help made cleaning the garage much faster.
A map is a great help when you are traveling.

easy.def: Ready to help.
examples: She is a helpful girl.
The map was helpful.
He is always helpful.

more.def: Giving help, or useful.
examples: The librarian was very helpful.
The map was helpful on our hike.
He is a helpful neighbor.

easy.def: Not able to help yourself.
examples: The baby is helpless.
A helpless kitten cried.
The turtle on its back was helpless.

more.def: Not able to take care of yourself or to do anything.
examples: A newborn baby is helpless.
The kitten was helpless in the tree.
The turtle felt helpless on its back.

easy.def: A word for a girl or a woman.
examples: I gave her a card.
Mom has her coat.
Tell her the news.

more.def: A word used for a girl, a woman, or a female animal, either as the one receiving an action or as the owner of something.
examples: We threw a party to thank her for the help.
Her bicycle has a bell and a basket.
The teacher asked her to read the poem aloud.

easy.def: In this place.
examples: Come here, please.
I live here.
Put the box here.

more.def: In or to the place where you are, or at this point in time.
examples: Our class has been here at the museum all morning.
Please bring your chair over here, next to the window.
Spring is here, and the flowers are blooming.

easy.def: A brave person who helps others.
examples: The firefighter is a hero.
My mom is my hero.
The hero in the story saves the town.

more.def: A person admired for being brave or for doing something great.
examples: She became a hero when she saved the child from the river.
The dog was called a hero for waking the family during the fire.
My hero is the scientist who found the cure.

easy.def: Belonging to her.
examples: The red coat is hers.
This book is hers.
Is the dog hers?

more.def: Used to show that something belongs to a girl or woman.
examples: The winning ticket was hers.
This pencil is mine, and that one is hers.
The prize was hers.

easy.def: She, and not someone else.
examples: She made lunch herself.
She hurt herself.
Mia sees herself in the mirror.

more.def: Used to talk about a girl or woman who has just been named, as the one who does or gets the action.
examples: She taught herself to play the guitar.
Maria made a cake all by herself.
The little girl dressed herself.

easy.def: To stop for a moment because you are not sure.
examples: I hesitate before I jump in the pool.
The cat hesitated at the door.
Do not hesitate to ask for help.

more.def: To pause before doing something because you feel unsure or nervous.
examples: He hesitated at the door, wondering if he should knock.
She hesitated before answering the hard question.
The deer hesitated at the edge of the road.
